metadata.description: Lebanese banking secrecy, monetary/credit law, anti-money laundering, and financial regulation

amendments.summary: Created Special Investigation Commission with authority to lift banking secrecy for money laundering investigations.
Updated anti-money laundering framework; expanded grounds for lifting secrecy.
Partially lifted banking secrecy for the benefit of forensic audit of the central bank and public institutions. Major reform in response to the financial crisis.

laws.historical_context: Inspired by the Swiss banking system, this law established Lebanon as a banking secrecy haven, attracting regional deposits and earning Lebanon the title 'Switzerland of the Middle East.' Absolute secrecy binds bank managers and employees from disclosing client names, assets, and transactions to any authority. Code-numbered accounts permitted. The law has been progressively weakened since 2001 through anti-money laundering legislation and the 2022 partial lifting during the financial crisis. However, significant secrecy protections remain, making forensic investigations of the banking sector challenging.

laws.official_title_french: Code de la Monnaie et du Crédit

amendments.summary: Amended bank licensing and capital requirements. Required Central Bank authorization for new banks.
Amended provisions related to central bank operations.

laws.historical_context: Established the Banque du Liban (BDL / مصرف لبنان) as Lebanon's central bank and defined the monetary policy framework. Replaced the previously existing currency board arrangement. Defines BDL's role in monetary stability, bank supervision, exchange rate policy, and lender of last resort functions. The Code became the subject of intense scrutiny during the post-2019 financial crisis, with debates about BDL's financial engineering operations, loss allocation, and the need for fundamental reform of the monetary system.

laws.official_title_arabic: قانون مكافحة تبييض الأموال وتمويل الإرهاب - قانون رقم 44/2015
laws.official_title_french: Loi No. 44/2015 - Lutte contre le Blanchiment d'Argent et le Financement du Terrorisme
laws.official_title_english: Law on Fighting Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing
laws.historical_context: Replaced Law No. 318/2001 (which itself replaced initial AML provisions). Expanded the mandate of the Special Investigation Commission (SIC), broadened predicate offenses, enhanced know-your-customer requirements, and aligned Lebanon with FATF recommendations. The SIC has exclusive authority to decide on lifting banking secrecy for AML/CFT investigations.

laws.official_number: Law No. 42 of November 24, 2015 (Cross-Border Cash Transportation)
laws.official_title_arabic: قانون التصريح عن نقل الأموال عبر الحدود - قانون رقم 42/2015
laws.official_title_french: Loi No. 42/2015 - Déclaration du Transport Transfrontalier de Fonds
laws.official_title_english: Law on Declaring Cross-Border Transportation of Money
laws.historical_context: Requires declaration of cash above a threshold when entering or leaving Lebanon. Part of the 2015 package of financial reform laws addressing FATF requirements.

laws.official_title_arabic: قانون تنظيم التداول بناء على معلومات غير معلنة - قانون رقم 160/2011
laws.historical_context: Prohibited insider trading using material non-public information. Part of efforts to develop Lebanon's capital markets framework.

laws.official_title_english: Financial Markets Law / Capital Markets Law
laws.historical_context: Established the Capital Markets Authority (CMA / هيئة الأسواق المالية) to regulate and supervise Lebanon's financial markets. Governs the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE), broker-dealer operations, and securities issuance.

laws.official_number: Decree No. 9976/1975 & Decree No. 29/1977 (Banking Free Zone)

amendments.summary: Removed income tax exemption on deposit interest for non-resident accounts.

laws.historical_context: Established a banking free zone exempting non-resident foreign currency deposits from certain taxes and reserve requirements. Designed to attract offshore banking activity to Beirut.
Authorized banks to open joint accounts with single-signature operation. Important for banking convenience and asset planning.

laws.official_number: Law No. 306 of October 18, 2022 (Amendments to Banking Secrecy)
laws.official_title_arabic: قانون رقم 306/2022 - تعديل قانون سرية المصارف
laws.official_title_french: Loi No. 306/2022 - Modification de la Loi sur le Secret Bancaire
laws.official_title_english: Amendment to Banking Secrecy Law (Partial Lifting)
laws.historical_context: Partially lifted banking secrecy for benefit of forensic audit of the Central Bank (BDL) and public institutions. A key reform demanded by the international community (IMF, World Bank, FATF) in the context of Lebanon's financial crisis. Also lifted secrecy for tax authorities, anti-corruption bodies, and judicial investigations into public funds. Landmark legislation representing a significant shift in Lebanon's banking secrecy tradition.

laws.official_number: Law No. 175 of May 29, 2020 (Capital Controls - attempted)
laws.official_title_french: Loi sur le Contrôle des Capitaux
laws.historical_context: In the context of Lebanon's 2019 financial crisis, banks imposed de facto capital controls without legal basis. Multiple draft capital controls laws were debated in Parliament from 2020 onward. The absence of a formal capital controls law while banks restricted withdrawals was widely criticized as illegal and unconstitutional. Note: actual passage/status of this law requires verification as multiple versions were debated.
